clinical_category: OnabotulinumtoxinA pharmacology - localized reduction of muscle activity in spasticity
blueprint_topic: Mechanism and focal therapeutic effect of botulinum toxin for spasticity
stem: A client receives intramuscular onabotulinumtoxinA (BOTOX) for focal spasticity. Which mechanism best explains the local reduction in muscle activity?

options.A: The toxin inhibits acetylcholine release at motor nerve terminals, producing partial chemical denervation of the injected muscle
options.B: The toxin stimulates acetylcholine release throughout the body, producing generalized muscle contraction
options.C: The injection directly repairs the underlying neurologic lesion that caused the spasticity
options.D: The toxin acts mainly by increasing systemic skeletal-muscle activity rather than affecting neuromuscular transmission at the treated site

rationale: A is correct. The current BOTOX prescribing information states that onabotulinumtoxinA blocks neuromuscular transmission by entering nerve terminals and inhibiting acetylcholine release. When injected intramuscularly at therapeutic doses, this produces partial chemical denervation and a localized reduction in muscle activity. The current label lists spasticity as an indication. B and D reverse the neuromuscular effect. C incorrectly treats focal symptom management as repair of the underlying neurologic disease. The final item does not claim that all effects remain strictly local, because the boxed warning notes that toxin effects can spread beyond the injection site in some patients.
educational_objective: Recognize that intramuscular onabotulinumtoxinA reduces focal spasticity by inhibiting acetylcholine release at motor nerve terminals and producing localized chemical denervation of treated muscle.
source_organization: National Library of Medicine (DailyMed; FDA-approved prescribing information)
source_version_date: Prescribing information revised 2026-02; current DailyMed label accessed 2026-08-18
source_locator: DailyMed current BOTOX label → Section 1.4 'Spasticity': indicated for treatment of spasticity in patients 2 years of age and older. Section 12.1 'Mechanism of Action': BOTOX blocks neuromuscular transmission by inhibiting acetylcholine release; intramuscular therapeutic injection produces partial chemical denervation and localized reduction in muscle activity. Boxed Warning/Section 5.1: toxin effects may spread from the injection area, so the mechanism should not be described as incapable of systemic spread.
source_claim_supported: The current February 2026 official BOTOX label directly supports acetylcholine-release inhibition, partial chemical denervation, localized reduction in treated-muscle activity, and the labeled spasticity indication while cautioning that toxin effects may spread beyond the injection site.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies client-needs subcategory (13–19% of items); this item tests medication mechanism and focal therapeutic effect in spasticity management.
correction_summary: Substantive refinement. The generic FDA landing page was replaced by the current February 2026 BOTOX label. The final item names onabotulinumtoxinA specifically and uses the exact acetylcholine-release/chemical-denervation mechanism, while correcting the source's implication that the effect is invariably restricted to the injection site by acknowledging the label's distant-spread warning.
audit_findings: The original generic FDA URL failed the exact-locator requirement.
Current February 2026 BOTOX labeling directly identifies spasticity as an indication and acetylcholine-release inhibition with partial chemical denervation as the intramuscular mechanism.
The source's phrase implying a purely local effect was narrowed because the official boxed warning recognizes possible distant spread of toxin effect.
Distractors reverse acetylcholine physiology or falsely claim repair of the underlying neurologic lesion; none is defensible.
Independent adversarial second pass found one uniquely correct answer, no unsupported duration or reinjection interval, no second answer, no cueing, and no unresolved conflict.
